title: Modals and Offcanvas
summary: A modal opens a box over the page. An offcanvas panel slides in from an edge.
introduction: A modal opens a box over the page. An offcanvas panel slides in from an edge. Use these only when they help the reader finish a task. Learn how to open, close and name each one, including for keyboard users.
learningObjectives: Build a modal from modal, modal-dialog and modal-content with a header, body and footer
Open and close modals and offcanvas panels with data attributes and with JavaScript
Size, centre and scroll modals, and place offcanvas panels on any edge
Explain what Bootstrap does for focus, Escape and the backdrop

blocks.text: A modal is three nested boxes. The outer `.modal` covers the viewport and is hidden until opened; `.modal-dialog` positions and sizes the dialog; `.modal-content` is the white box with the header, body and footer. The outer element needs `tabindex="-1"` so Bootstrap can move focus to it, `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title, and `aria-hidden="true"` while closed. Any element with `data-bs-toggle="modal"` and a `data-bs-target` naming the modal's id opens it; any element inside with `data-bs-dismiss="modal"` closes it.

blocks.title: A sign-up dialog
blocks.code: Join the Garden Club

blocks.title: Behaviour in the browser (bundle required)
blocks.content:
On load: only the "Join the club" button is visible
Click it: the page dims under a 50% black backdrop and a white dialog, 500px wide, fades in near the top of the window, showing the title, an × button, the email field and two footer buttons
Focus moves into the dialog and Tab cycles only through its controls; the page behind cannot scroll
Escape, a click on the backdrop, × and Cancel all close it; "Send invitation" does nothing yet

blocks.text: Everything in that last two lines, the backdrop, the scroll lock, the focus trap and the Escape key, is done by Bootstrap. You wrote none of it, which is the reason to use the component rather than a hand-rolled `<div>` with `display: none`.
Sizes, centring, scrolling and a static backdrop

Modifier classes on `.modal-dialog` change the dialog; data attributes on `.modal` change the behaviour. The defaults suit a short form; long terms-and-conditions text wants a large, scrollable, centred dialog that the user cannot dismiss by accident.

rows: Max width 300px, 800px or 1140px instead of the default 500px
Fill the viewport always, or only below a breakpoint
Centre the dialog vertically instead of placing it near the top
Scroll the body inside the dialog instead of the whole dialog
Clicking the backdrop no longer closes the modal
Escape no longer closes the modal

blocks.title: A large, centred, scrollable modal that must be closed with a button
blocks.code:
Membership terms

Long terms text goes here…

blocks.title: Behaviour in the browser
blocks.content:
An 800px wide dialog centred vertically in the window; if the terms are taller than the window, only the body scrolls while the header and footer stay put
Clicking the backdrop or pressing Escape does nothing; only "I agree" closes it

blocks.text: Data attributes cover "open on click". For anything else, such as opening a dialog after a timer or when a form fails, create an instance and call its methods. Since 5.2 the constructor accepts a selector string or an element. Every component also emits events you can listen for; `shown.bs.modal` fires once the fade-in has finished, which is the right moment to put the cursor in a field.

blocks.title: Opening the sign-up modal with code
Behaviour in the browser
blocks.content:
Clicking the element with id openSignup opens the dialog exactly as the data attribute did
As soon as the fade-in completes, the cursor is blinking in the email field

blocks.text: The instance also has `hide()`, `toggle()` and `dispose()`. If a data attribute may already have created an instance for the same element, use `bootstrap.Modal.getOrCreateInstance(modalElement)` instead of `new`, so you do not end up with two controllers fighting over one dialog. The four lifecycle events are `show`, `shown`, `hide` and `hidden`, each suffixed with `.bs.modal`.

Offcanvas uses the same ideas with different class names: `.offcanvas` plus a placement class (`offcanvas-start`, `offcanvas-end`, `offcanvas-top`, `offcanvas-bottom`), a header with a title and a `btn-close` with `data-bs-dismiss="offcanvas"`, and a body. It is 400px wide (or 30vh tall for top and bottom) and slides in over a backdrop. Typical uses are mobile navigation, filter panels and shopping carts.

blocks.title: A filter panel from the right edge
blocks.code: Filter plants

blocks.title: Behaviour in the browser
blocks.content:
Click "Filters": a 400px wide white panel slides in from the right edge over a dimmed backdrop, showing the title, × and the two checkboxes
Escape, the backdrop or × slide it back out; the page does not scroll while it is open

blocks.text: Two attributes adjust the behaviour: `data-bs-scroll="true"` keeps the page scrollable behind the panel and `data-bs-backdrop="false"` removes the backdrop. A **responsive offcanvas** uses `offcanvas-lg` (or another breakpoint) instead of plain `offcanvas`: below that width the content behaves as a sliding panel, and from the breakpoint up it is rendered in place as ordinary content, which is how a sidebar can double as a mobile drawer.

blocks.title: Common mistake: a modal nested inside a positioned parent
blocks.text: Modals and offcanvas should be direct children of `<body>`, or at least outside any element that has `position: fixed`, `transform`, `filter` or `overflow: hidden`. Placed inside a fixed navbar or a card with `overflow: hidden`, the dialog is clipped, appears in the wrong place or sits beneath its own backdrop. Move the markup to the end of the body; the trigger button can stay wherever it is, because the connection is made by id.

blocks.title: Return focus is automatic
blocks.text: When a modal or offcanvas closes, Bootstrap moves focus back to the element that opened it. Open dialogs from a real `<button>`, not a `<div>` with a click handler, so keyboard users can open them in the first place and land somewhere sensible afterwards.

questions.question: Which class centres the dialog vertically in the window?
questions.explanation: modal-dialog-centered goes on .modal-dialog. modal-lg changes width, modal-dialog-scrollable changes scrolling, and modal-fullscreen fills the viewport.

questions.question: In a left-to-right page, `offcanvas-end` slides the panel in from the right edge.
questions.explanation: start and end follow the writing direction: in LTR pages start is the left edge and end is the right edge. In RTL pages they swap.
